counterexample.note: The compressed start (0) is bit 0 of word 0, so the repair loads word -1 instead, and the first search reads bit 0 of the wrong word and misses tick 0. Active liquidity is 1000 at tick 30 and 0 at tick -30. Aligned initialized start ticks are also still skipped, as in the audited code: tick spacing 10, position [100, 200), start 100, end 0 returns nothing.

new_flaw.description: For an unaligned start tick whose compressed position is bit 0 of a word, reset loads the word below instead of the start's own word. The first search then reads bit 0 of the wrong word, so it can skip an initialized tick that the audited code handled correctly.
new_flaw.scenario: Tick spacing 60, pool tick 30, and tick 0 is the lower tick of an in-range position. The first taxed zero-for-one swap in a block moves the price to tick -30. The walk skips tick 0, so the hook keeps using the liquidity from above tick 0 for the range below it. This is the same liquidity mismatch as the original finding: depending on the net liquidity at tick 0, the swap reverts on a later subtraction or the tax is divided by the wrong liquidity.

summary: For an unaligned start tick, reset loads the bitmap word of the compressed start minus one, then calls _advanceToNextDown from the start tick as before. Aligned initialized start ticks are still skipped, and when the compressed start is bit 0 of a word the first search reads the wrong word.
